name: Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars

podcast.body: This album was a huge seller in England through late 1972 and into 1973, complete with hit singles. It was central to Bowie's immense popularity and the widespread fascination with his Ziggy Stardust alter-ego during an extraordinary 18 months in British rock history. "His album Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders for Mars was a huge seller, complete with all the required hits singles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, released on June 16, 1972, features one of the most famous album covers of the 1970s, depicting Bowie posing on Heddon Street in London. A conspiracy theory suggests this album cover and its contents predict the rise of Kanye West. "One of the most famous album covers of the 1970s is what we see on the front of Bowie's Ziggy start us in the spiders from Mars album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Album
podcast.body: This record, released in 1972, is consistently held in higher and higher esteem with each passing year, and is cited as a groundbreaking and influential work in music history. It introduced themes of dystopianism and dread that would be revisited later in his career. "Damn, that's an influential record."
